variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Apache Cassandra is a distributed wide-column database built to keep partition-key reads and writes available across a peer cluster. A client can send a request to any node. That node becomes the coordinator for the request, finds the replicas for the partition, and waits for the number of responses required by the chosen consistency level.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Partition key
pairs.detail: The partition key is hashed to a token.
pairs.explanation: The partition key is hashed to a token. It chooses the logical partition and, through the keyspace replication strategy, the nodes that store copies of that partition.

pairs.label: Clustering columns
pairs.detail: Clustering columns order rows inside one partition.
pairs.explanation: Clustering columns order rows inside one partition. They support bounded slices after the query provides the partition key; they do not redistribute a hot partition.

pairs.label: Query projection
pairs.detail: One business fact may be copied into several tables so each important query has a direct key path.
pairs.explanation: One business fact may be copied into several tables so each important query has a direct key path. The application owns the write fan-out and reconciliation between those projections.

variants.hint:
Partition key: The partition key is hashed to a token.

Clustering columns: Clustering columns order rows inside one partition.

Query projection: One business fact may be copied into several tables so each important query has a direct key path.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

pairs.label: Hash the key
pairs.detail: Hash the complete partition key to one token.
pairs.explanation: Hash the complete partition key to one token. Token-aware drivers can route toward a replica, but any contacted node can coordinate the request.

pairs.label: Find token owners
pairs.detail: Locate the range containing the token.
pairs.explanation: Locate the range containing the token. Virtual tokens let each physical node own many ranges so growth and failure load can be distributed.

pairs.label: Choose replicas
pairs.detail: Apply the datacenter RF and rack topology.
pairs.explanation: Apply the datacenter RF and rack topology. Confirm that the infrastructure labels represent independent power, network, or availability-zone failures.

pairs.label: Wait for responses
pairs.detail: Send the operation to replicas and return only after the selected consistency level's acknowledgement condition is met or the request times out.
pairs.explanation: Send the operation to replicas and return only after the selected consistency level's acknowledgement condition is met or the request times out.

pairs.label: Hints
pairs.detail: A coordinator can retain a hint for a missed replica and replay it after that replica returns.
pairs.explanation: A coordinator can retain a hint for a missed replica and replay it after that replica returns. Hints shorten common outages, but they are best effort and are not a substitute for repair.

pairs.label: Repair
pairs.detail: Repair compares replicas for common token ranges, uses Merkle trees to locate differences, and streams missing data.
pairs.explanation: Repair compares replicas for common token ranges, uses Merkle trees to locate differences, and streams missing data. It consumes disk, CPU, and network I/O, so its schedule is part of capacity planning.

pairs.label: Tombstone safety
pairs.detail: A delete writes a timestamped tombstone.
pairs.explanation: A delete writes a timestamped tombstone. Purging it before an old live value has been repaired can allow deleted data to reappear when that stale replica returns.

pairs.label: Append for recovery
pairs.detail: Record the mutation in an append-oriented log according to the configured sync policy.
pairs.explanation: Record the mutation in an append-oriented log according to the configured sync policy. After a crash, the node can replay accepted mutations not yet flushed.

pairs.label: Update memory
pairs.detail: Apply the mutation to the table's sorted in-memory structure so current data can participate in reads before flush.
pairs.explanation: Apply the mutation to the table's sorted in-memory structure so current data can participate in reads before flush.

pairs.label: Flush immutable files
pairs.detail: Write a memtable to immutable SSTable components.
pairs.explanation: Write a memtable to immutable SSTable components. Updates and tombstones for one partition may now exist across several SSTables.

pairs.label: Merge in background
pairs.detail: Read and rewrite selected SSTables, reconcile versions, and discard data only when Cassandra can do so safely.
pairs.explanation: Read and rewrite selected SSTables, reconcile versions, and discard data only when Cassandra can do so safely. This creates write amplification and consumes I/O headroom.

variants.prompt: Why can TimeWindowCompactionStrategy fit TTL-based time-series data?
options: It turns every query into a cross-partition join
It groups data by time window so SSTables whose contents expire together can be removed efficiently
It eliminates write amplification and repair
It makes out-of-order timestamps irrelevant
